ai.definition: AI-driven RPA solutions leverage artificial intelligence to automate repetitive tasks in various business processes, enhancing efficiency and reducing human error.
ai.howItWorks: These solutions utilize machine learning algorithms to recognize patterns, make decisions, and execute actions based on predefined rules. They can interact with software interfaces, databases, and other systems as a human would, but without the need for manual intervention.
ai.problemSolved: Repetitive and time-consuming business tasks that are prone to human error, such as data entry, form filling, and document processing.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing AI models, integrating them with existing RPA tools, and deploying these solutions in enterprise environments. This often requires custom software development and integration with legacy systems.
ai.buildProcess: Involves gathering requirements from stakeholders, designing workflows, training the AI model on specific tasks, and testing the solution before full-scale deployment.
ai.costDrivers: Includes development costs for AI models, licensing fees for RPA tools, and ongoing maintenance and support expenses. Training data acquisition can also be a significant cost driver.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Gaining traction in enterprise environments but still maturing towards widespread adoption.
ai.regulation: Subject to varying regulations depending on the industry and geographical location, particularly concerning data privacy and security. Compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, or other relevant laws is crucial.
ai.risks: Includes risks related to data breaches, AI model bias, and integration challenges with legacy systems. There are also concerns about job displacement and ethical implications of AI in business processes.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability due to increased efficiency and cost savings, but initial investment can be significant.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected growth driven by advancements in AI technology, expanding use cases across industries, and increasing demand from businesses looking to optimize operations.

glossary.def: The development of computer systems that can perform tasks requiring human-like intelligence, such as learning, problem-solving, and decision-making.
A software technology used to automate repetitive business processes by mimicking the actions of a human user in a digital environment.
A subset of AI that involves training algorithms to make predictions or decisions based on data, enabling systems to improve their performance over time without explicit programming.

subsystems.name: Bot runtime and orchestrator
subsystems.role: executes automations on a schedule or event, and queues work items between them.

subsystems.name: Interface adapters
subsystems.role: let software act like a human user across old and new systems.

subsystems.name: Document understanding
subsystems.role: turns scanned forms, invoices and emails into structured fields.

subsystems.name: Decision layer
subsystems.role: handles the judgement calls that plain rules cannot.

subsystems.name: Human-in-the-loop console
subsystems.role: review queues where people approve, correct or take over.

subsystems.name: Governance and audit
subsystems.role: keeps automated changes traceable and within policy.

buildSteps.title: Mine the process
buildSteps.detail: Event logs from the systems involved are analysed, and employee screen activity is recorded, to reconstruct how a task is really done and how often it varies.

buildSteps.title: Select and scope
buildSteps.detail: High-volume, rules-heavy, stable tasks with digital inputs are chosen; anything needing frequent human judgement stays out of the first wave.

buildSteps.title: Model the workflow
buildSteps.detail: Each step, decision point, exception and system of record is written down, and the target straight-through processing rate is set.

buildSteps.title: Train the document models
buildSteps.detail: Several hundred to a few thousand representative documents are annotated, extraction models trained, and accuracy measured per field, not just overall.

buildSteps.title: Build the bot
buildSteps.detail: Actions are scripted or recorded against each interface, API calls replace screen actions where possible, and credentials are stored in the vault rather than in the script.

buildSteps.title: Test against reality
buildSteps.detail: Runs are shadowed alongside human workers on live queues, deliberately fed malformed inputs, and checked for correct exception handling before any write access is granted.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with human review
buildSteps.detail: The bot processes confident cases automatically and sends low-confidence ones to a review queue, with volumes ramped up gradually.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Straight-through rates, error types and model drift are tracked continuously; UI changes, new form layouts and new exception classes force scheduled rebuilding.

prerequisites.tech: Digital systems of record with usable interfaces
prerequisites.why: a bot can only drive screens, APIs or files that exist and are reachable.
most business inputs arrive as PDFs, scans and emails rather than clean data.
bots need scheduled, scalable, isolated execution with central logging.
software acting as an employee needs the same access controls and traceability.

prerequisites.tech: Reliable language models for unstructured tasks
prerequisites.why: handling free-form emails and unexpected documents still needs review, and output must be constrained to be dependable.

pathway.milestone: rules-based bots with OCR on structured forms in finance, insurance and shared-service centres
pathway.unlocks: lower cost and fewer keystroke errors on high-volume back-office work.

pathway.milestone: combined automation plus machine-learning decisioning, with measured straight-through rates and human review only for exceptions
pathway.unlocks: automation of tasks that need classification or judgement, not just rule-following.

pathway.milestone: agent-style workflows where a language model plans steps across several systems under tight guardrails
pathway.unlocks: semi-structured and long-tail tasks that were previously uneconomic to automate.

pathway.milestone: self-monitoring automations that detect interface drift, re-learn and request approval for changed behaviour
pathway.unlocks: lower maintenance burden, which is the main reason automation programmes stall.
